evals.prompt: I need one skill to upload through the Agent Skills API and another project-local Claude Code skill that uses arguments, paths, and load-time shell. Author and validate both without pretending the formats are identical.
evals.expected_output: Two explicit profiles with portable-only metadata for upload and validated Claude Code extensions/injection for the local skill.
expectations: Uses only the six portable frontmatter fields for the upload skill and requires name/description.
Uses --mode portable and --mode claude-code explicitly in validation commands.
Treats dynamic injection as Claude Code-only and keeps invocation arguments out of shell source.
Validates extension field types and combinations such as fork-only agent/background.

evals.prompt: Add output evals for a skill named api-review. There are no fixture files. I want checks that can be graded from the response rather than the model's hidden reasoning.
evals.expected_output: A valid evals/evals.json object with matching skill_name, positive integer IDs, empty files arrays, and observable expectations.
expectations: Uses the official object schema with skill_name and a non-empty evals array.
Each eval includes a positive integer id, prompt, expected_output, optional files, and a non-empty expectations array.
Uses files: [] instead of a nonexistent placeholder fixture.
Expectations target observable output/actions and IDs are unique.

evals.prompt: Update the skill-authoring guidance for this repository's npm package. Tell users exactly what the current Node installer and uninstaller do, including project paths and .agents support.
evals.expected_output: Documentation matching bin/cli.js and lib ownership rather than a generic --all/--group installer design.
expectations: Documents the interactive install and install/uninstall/help flags currently implemented.
States that global/project targets are ~/.claude and <project>/.claude and that the Node flow does not mirror .agents.
States that Node uninstall removes only manifest-recorded global items and preserves project installs, keys, dependencies, and bulk installs.
Does not claim --all, --group, --dry-run, or project uninstall exists.

evals.prompt: Audit this Claude Code skill line: `!`deploy --target "$ARGUMENTS"``. The author says quoting makes it safe and deploy only reads status unless a flag is present.
evals.expected_output: A violation finding that keeps invocation text and the potentially mutating command out of load-time shell.
expectations: Explains that skill argument substitution is textual and happens before shell execution, so shell quotes do not provide argv escaping.
Treats load-time execution as unconditional and rejects the possibly mutating deploy command.
Moves validation and execution to a normal tool call while leaving invocation text in prompt content.

evals.prompt: A reviewer rejected `root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` inside one fenced injection because dynamic injection is single-pass. They also split a dependent second command into a new placeholder. Correct the review.
evals.expected_output: A correction distinguishing renderer recursion from normal shell command substitution and requiring dependent reads to share one guarded block.
expectations: States that single-pass means inserted stdout is not rescanned for injection markers.
Allows normal shell command substitution inside one injection.
Treats separate placeholders as independent/unordered and potentially concurrent.
Keeps dependent commands sequential in one fenced shell script.

evals.prompt: Review this readiness injection: `!`cat ~/.config/service.json 2>/dev/null | head -20 || echo missing``. It runs for a personal skill in every repository.
evals.expected_output: A secret-safe, bounded status probe with a guard around the failing read rather than a misleading pipeline fallback.
expectations: Identifies that the final pipeline stage may hide the read failure without pipefail.
Rejects injecting configuration contents that may contain credentials and reports presence/status only.
Provides one short stdout fallback and redirects expected diagnostics.
Notes that policy-disabled shell must leave the surrounding skill coherent.
